## Research context

The historical study examined training stability and predictive-performance
variation across repeated initializations of an R-native neural network, with
Keras as a comparison framework. Two recorded batches contain 500 seed IDs each:
1–500 and 501–1,000. Their combination formed the 1,000-seed historical summary.
These experiments were important development milestones, not a current validation
of standard AdaGrad or evidence that DDESONN outperforms Keras.

The artifacts support the use of two batches to form the composite, but do not
record why two separate executions were chosen rather than one 1,000-seed job.
The original operational reason and statistical independence are not established
by the saved metric tables alone.

## Which AdaGrad was used?

The archived DDESONN script selects `optimizer = "adagrad"` and `ML_NN = TRUE`.
The corresponding archived multilayer code first subtracts a direct gradient
update, then subtracts an adaptive AdaGrad update from the same weights. That
custom double-update path is not standard AdaGrad. Its bias path also uses
summed layer errors rather than the current bias-gradient update.

The development name `adagrad_x` was considered for compatibility. It is not an
active optimizer in 7.3.0. The package uses corrected standard AdaGrad; neither
the legacy behavior nor its old optimizer state should be reused for new runs.
The saved results do not embed a source commit, so the exact executable state of
each original run cannot be certified from those artifacts.

## Historical measurements, not a new comparison

The following values describe archived evidence; no models were retrained to
produce this table. DDESONN values are computed from the two saved test-metric
tables (500 rows each). Keras values are transcribed from the workbook's Sheet2,
which reports 1,000 observations. Values are fractions, not percentages.

| Archived test-accuracy statistic | Legacy DDESONN | Keras workbook |
|:--|--:|--:|
| Count | 1,000 | 1,000 |
| Mean | 0.999218731 | 0.996808557 |
| Sample standard deviation | 0.001256088 | 0.003569493 |
| Minimum | 0.992000000 | 0.978667000 |
| Maximum | 1.000000000 | 1.000000000 |

These are legacy experimental observations, not evidence that correctly
implemented standard AdaGrad outperforms Keras. Their applicability depends on
optimizer semantics, preprocessing, splits, model selection and execution details
that have not all been reconstructed. The old summary helper selected maximum
accuracy within seed groups; each retained test table currently contains one row
per seed, but that approach should not be used to select future models on test
accuracy. No claim of clinical, deployment or general predictive reliability is
made from this small historical record.

## Seeds: what is known and unknown

The committed DDESONN benchmark script already includes `set.seed(111)`, a
configured `seeds <- 501:1000`, and `set.seed(s)` inside the experiment loop.
Those statements already appear in the first dedicated benchmark-path snapshot,
`1a41c9fe0c8e74190137370a2d507a7865b6bcae`, under
`helpfulFiles/vKeras/1000SEEDSRESULTSvkeras/`. Later revisions moved the same
script through development/data folders into `inst/scripts/`. The two RDS batches
retain disjoint seed labels. This contradicts treating the old vignette's claim that the runs
had no master seed as an established fact.

However, the saved results do not contain the original session's RNG state,
complete configuration, software versions or source revision. The available
script may differ from the exact version executed when the artifacts were
created. The history inspected does not show a transition from an unseeded
benchmark script to a seeded one. We therefore cannot determine whether the
original executions used that master seed, and do not call them unseeded or
irreproducible.

The archived Python script has master/per-run seed settings too, but its literal
`range(1, 1)` loop executes zero runs. It cannot reproduce the workbook as written.
The loop and local dataset path would require deliberate configuration; the
workbook alone does not prove the historical Python execution settings.

## Retrieve the historical research

Raw metrics, the available per-observation predictions, the workbook and historical
experiment scripts remain unchanged in Git. They are excluded from the 7.3.0
source package and installation, so this vignette deliberately does not load
RDS or Excel files with `system.file()`.

Use the immutable archive revision
[0d1b557098b56b39ed2357b30716dcddc25871b3](https://github.com/MatHatter/DDESONN/tree/0d1b557098b56b39ed2357b30716dcddc25871b3):

```sh
# From a repository clone that contains the archived history:
mkdir -p ../ddesonn-legacy-research
git archive 0d1b557098b56b39ed2357b30716dcddc25871b3 \
  inst/extdata/heart_failure_runs \
  inst/scripts/vsKeras/1000SEEDSRESULTSvsKeras \
  vignettes/DDESONNvsKeras_1000Seeds.Rmd \
  | tar -x -C ../ddesonn-legacy-research
```

The archive contains four compact train/test metric RDS files, one larger
run2 prediction RDS, the Keras workbook, and four research scripts. The run1
prediction RDS is absent from that compact archive, but remains recoverable from
older revision `4bc994462612ce868b90bc70885eb1635eddcdee`:

```sh
git show 4bc994462612ce868b90bc70885eb1635eddcdee:inst/extdata/heart_failure_runs/run1/SingleRun_Pretty_Test_Metrics_500_seeds_20251025.rds > ../ddesonn-legacy-research/run1-predictions.rds
```

It contains 375,000 prediction rows for seeds 1–500. Older revision
`1a41c9fe0c8e74190137370a2d507a7865b6bcae` also preserves per-seed metadata under
`inst/extdata/sample_runs/heart_failure_single_runs/`. Two inspected metadata
samples record learning rate 0.125, 360 epochs and one network, but omit or leave
NULL several other settings and do not record master RNG state or source commit.
These partial records do not settle the original master-seed question.
The research scripts are session-oriented historical material, not supported
package entry points or a turnkey reproduction of the original execution.

A detailed provenance audit, file hashes and a reproduction script for the
historical summary are kept under `dev/research/` in the repository. No historical
commits or raw observations have been rewritten.

## Future comparisons

Use corrected implementations and matched datasets, splits, preprocessing,
architecture, training budgets, tuning budgets and evaluation metrics. Start
with 10–30 seeds for exploration; consider 100 for a larger stability study,
and increase the count when measured variability or desired precision warrants
it. Record exact seeds, source revisions, software versions, optimizer settings
and checkpoint-selection rules. Report means, sample standard deviations,
uncertainty intervals and distributions, including failures and poor runs.
Small seed counts do not establish statistical superiority. Parallel execution
is deferred to future development and is not implemented for 7.3.0.
